subject: General Knowledge
topic: UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India

questions.stem: Which iconic white marble mausoleum located in Agra is arguably India's most famous and globally recognized UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal, built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 for being 'the jewel of Muslim art in India'.

questions.stem: The ancient rock-cut caves of Ajanta and Ellora, famous worldwide for their magnificent ancient Indian paintings and sculptures, are geographically located in which state?
questions.explanation: Both the Ajanta Caves (primarily Buddhist) and the Ellora Caves (a mix of Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain monuments) are UNESCO World Heritage Sites located near Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad) in Maharashtra.

questions.stem: Which specific UNESCO World Heritage Site in Northeast India is globally famous for hosting the world's largest population of the great one-horned rhinoceros?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park in Assam was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1985 for its unique natural environment. It is the primary sanctuary for the highly endangered one-horned rhinoceros.

questions.stem: The magnificent group of monuments at Hampi, officially recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site, served as the opulent capital of which great ancient Indian empire?
questions.explanation: Hampi, located in east-central Karnataka, was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th century. The ruins of the city, spread over a vast area, include the famous Virupaksha Temple and Vitthala Temple.

questions.stem: The incredibly distinct architectural work of which famous Swiss-French modernist architect, located in Chandigarh, was officially recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016?
questions.explanation: UNESCO designated 'The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier, an Outstanding Contribution to the Modern Movement' as a World Heritage Site. This includes the Capitol Complex in Chandigarh, which is considered a masterpiece of brutalist architecture.
